mechanism: Detect swing highs/lows as bars whose high/low dominates neighbors within length L (coded L=5–20). Valid Break of Structure only when prior bar close (body) breaks the stored swing: Bid>swing_H and close(1)>swing_H for bullish BoS; Ask<swing_L and close(1)<swing_L for bearish. Wick-only pierces are invalid. Distinguishes BoS (continuation HH/HL or LL/LH) from MSS (shift without prior opposite break) and CHoCH (character change after opposite swing break).
data_needed: OHLC series; swing_H/swing_L state; length/limit window; body close of bar 1; Ask/Bid.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; strategy text prefers HTF (H4/D1) for structure and optional M5 for confirmation; tester uses chart period.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an SMC structure-break change sensor gated on candle-body close through swing extremes, with explicit invalidation of wick breaks and taxonomy vs MSS/CHoCH.
quote: only breaks on candle or bar bodies are considered valid Breaks of Structures, meaning that breaks on candle tails, shadows, or wicks, are considered invalid Breaks of Structures

mechanism: After valid BoS, classify regime by swing sequence: bullish BoS in uptrend = new HH after HL pattern; bearish BoS in downtrend = new LL after LH pattern. HTF structure scan avoids LTF noise from liquidity sweeps.
data_needed: Labeled swing sequence (HH/HL/LH/LL); HTF OHLC; BoS events.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex generic; HTF H4/D1 recommended for trend; entry on break of swing.
why_new_for_mis: Maps SMC swing taxonomy into an explicit trend-regime state (HH/HL vs LH/LL) driven by validated BoS events.
quote: Uptrends contain patterns of higher highs and higher lows in price action, while downtrends consist of lower lows and lower highs patterns.

mechanism: EA tutorial: RSI 30/70 cross opens seed trade then hedges with doubling lots inside fixed zoneRange/zoneTarget point bands until target exit. Execution/recovery system, not a market-structure sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/PERIOD_CURRENT; RSI(14); zoneRange=200 pts, zoneTarget=400 pts.
why_new_for_mis: No new MIS market sensing after full read—position-recovery martingale with RSI trigger only.
quote: the zone recovery martingale strategy is a common strategy that is aimed at countering losing positions by opening opposite positions with a slightly greater trading volume

mechanism: On visible chart bars only: CopyHigh/CopyLow, sort, keep top-10 highs and bottom-10 lows. Nested scan finds non-adjacent bars (≥10 bars apart) whose highs (or lows) match within ≤10 points; confirmed pairs become horizontal resistance/support levels drawn as HLINEs. Levels deleted when no longer among visible extremes.
data_needed: Visible-bar OHLC via ChartGetInteger(CHART_VISIBLE_BARS); sorted extreme arrays; point tolerance 10.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; pure price-action on visible window.
why_new_for_mis: Adaptive horizontal S/R regime sensor from repeated round-number extremes on the visible window, with proximity expiry—usable as liquidity-pool / balance-level context for MIS.
quote: CHECK FOR RESISTANCE ... high_diff <= 10 ... CHECK FOR SUPPORT ... low_diff <= 10

mechanism: Fade-the-break sensor: sell when prior bar opens below resistance, wicks above it (high>R), closes bearish (open>close), and Bid back below R; buy when prior bar opens above support, wicks below it, closes bullish, and Ask back above S. One signal per level via static traded-price latch.
data_needed: Active S/R object prices; open1/high1/low1/close1; Ask/Bid; per-level trade latch.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit false-break / liquidity-sweep change sensor on horizontal S/R (reject after pierce), complementary to true-breakout sensors.
quote: we will fade the break. We will open buy positions when we break the supports and open sell positions when we break the resistance levels.

mechanism: Supervised PatchTST: segment OHLC into patches (patch_len=24, stride=24), RevIN normalize against distribution shift (x=(x-mean)/std + optional affine), series-decompose to trend+residual, channel-independent Transformer encoder, flatten head → denorm forecast. Context 168 H1 bars → predict next 24 H1 OHLC bars; ONNX in MQL5 draws future bars once per hour.
data_needed: EURUSD H1 OHLC (~80k bars train); seq_len=168; pred_len=24; 4 features O/H/L/C; ONNX model buffer.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 primary; code also supports M1/M5/M15/D1 fetch.
why_new_for_mis: Patch-based Transformer with RevIN + trend/residual decomposition as a multi-horizon OHLC sequence sensor for MIS—forecasts full candle paths, not a scalar direction score.
quote: RevIn attempts to tackle the problem of distribution shift in time-series forecasting.

mechanism: Each tick: HistorySelect today's DEAL_ENTRY_OUT deals; sum profit+commission+swap → daily_PnL%; startingBalance = balance − total_day_Profit. Gate isTradeAllowed=false when daily_PnL% ≤ −5% OR equity vs initialBalance ≤ −12%. Dashboard updates day window and color-coded DD state.
data_needed: Account balance/equity; HistoryDeals for calendar day; initialBalance at OnInit; dayBalance at day rollover.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Account-level (any symbol chart attach); demo random trades on chart symbol.
why_new_for_mis: Prop-style dual drawdown regime sensor (intraday closed-PnL% + lifetime equity DD%) that can inhibit all trading—account-risk sensing layer for MIS, not a price indicator.

mechanism: EMA(10)/EMA(20) crossover opens seed trade then cascades add-ons and trails SL when price hits stepped TP—order-management tutorial, not a novel market sensor.
why_new_for_mis: No new MIS sensing after full read—standard EMA cross with cascade position scaling.
quote: A cascade order strategy involves the consecutive initiation of transactions in response to the predetermined events or conditions.

mechanism: On new bar if no active range: over last rangeBars (10) find highest high and lowest low; valid consolidation iff (HH−LL)/_Point ≤ rangeSizePoints (400). Plot expanding rectangle; while in-range, extend end time each bar and update HH/LL if Ask/Bid push extremes—live low-volatility box sensor.
data_needed: iHighest/iLowest over rangeBars; PRICE1_Y1/PRICE2_Y2; rangeSizePoints; isRangeExist/isInRange flags.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; example validity ~10 bars within 400 points (text also cites 700 pts/70 pips).
why_new_for_mis: Explicit low-volatility consolidation regime detector with max-range-in-points criterion and live box growth—direct MIS quiet-market / balance-phase sensor.
quote: isInRange = (PRICE1_Y1 - PRICE2_Y2)/_Point <= rangeSizePoints; // Check if the range size is within the allowed points

mechanism: While in consolidation: high-break price = LL + rangeSizePoints*_Point; low-break = HH − rangeSizePoints*_Point. Ask > high-break → bullish breakout; Bid < low-break → bearish. Reset range flags after break.
data_needed: Active box HH/LL; rangeSizePoints; Ask/Bid each tick.
why_new_for_mis: Breakout change sensor keyed off the consolidation's own max-width envelope (not just HH/LL touch)—fires when price expands beyond the allowed quiet-range size.
quote: A breakout occurs when the price closes above the resistance level or below the support level.

mechanism: BB middle=SMA(period), upper/lower = SMA ± BandDeviation*StdDev (defaults period 30, deviation 2). Band squeeze (bands constrict) flags low-volatility compression preceding expansion; price < lower → oversold/buy mean-reversion cue; price > upper → overbought/sell cue.
why_new_for_mis: Classic but concrete vol-compression (squeeze) plus band-extreme sensors for MIS volatility regime and reversion triggers.
quote: The "band squeeze," which happens as the bands constrict and converge closer together ... suggests a time of low volatility and may also portend the impending occurrence of a big price move or breakout.

mechanism: RSI(7) with asymmetric thresholds: oversold <15 and prior close > SMA(25) → buy; overbought >35 and prior close < SMA(25) → sell. Aggressive short-period RSI band plus MA trend filter; trailing stop 25 pts.
data_needed: iRSI(7); iMA(25 SMA close); Close[1]; Ask/Bid.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY H1 backtest cited; also EURUSD/USDJPY noted as suited.
why_new_for_mis: Non-standard RSI sensing band (15/35 on period 7) gated by SMA regime—faster exhaustion sensor than classic 30/70×14 for MIS momentum extremes.
quote: the EA will employ a brief 7-day RSI timeframe, with thresholds set at 35 for overbought and 15 for oversold circumstances.

mechanism: In StartDate–EndDate window find max high and min low; later extremum is primary fan origin, earlier is opposite fan. From each origin draw nine rays at 82.5°,75°,71.25°,63.75°,45°,26.25°,18.75°,15°,7.5° (1x8…8x1) via endPrice=extremum±tan(angle)*300*_Point, ray-right. Price above/below 1x1 and interaction with steeper/flatter angles sense trend strength and dynamic S/R.
data_needed: High/low/time arrays in date range; ArrayMaximum/Minimum; OBJ_TREND fans; chart scale awareness.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any chart symbol/period; user StartDate/EndDate; PeriodSeconds()*300 forward span.
why_new_for_mis: Dual Gann-fan geometric regime/S/R sensor from paired extrema—multi-angle time-price balance lines as alternate structure layer for MIS (Part I indicator only).
quote: a 45 degree angle (known as the 1x1 angle) represented the perfect balance between time and price.

mechanism: iSAR(step=0.02, max=0.2): if prior close > SAR → uptrend/buy regime; if prior close < SAR → downtrend/sell regime. Dots below price = uptrend, above = downtrend; step/max control acceleration toward price.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY M1 backtest 2024.01–2024.08; also EURUSD suited, GBPUSD poor per author.
why_new_for_mis: Stop-and-reverse trail as a binary trend-regime sensor (price vs accelerating SAR) for MIS directional state.
quote: When the dots are below the price, the market is in an uptrend; when they are above, the market is downtrend.

mechanism: On D1, for chosen MonthToShow over YearsToShow (10–15): for each year compute month P/L as last-day open − first-day open (points-aware). Hit-rate of same-direction years: ≥75% → Strong trend, 60–75% Moderate, <60% Flat. Overlay olive multi-year average path vs yellow current-year path.
data_needed: D1 opens for Symbol1 (and optional Symbol2) across years; MonthToShow; YearsToShow; FillGaps.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: D1: SP500, GBPJPY, AUDNZD, AUDUSD, GBPUSD, NZDUSD, WTI, XAGUSD, NQ100; months Jun/Jul/Aug/Apr/Nov/Jan/Dec examples.
why_new_for_mis: Calendar-month multi-year hit-rate regime sensor with Strong/Moderate/Flat labels—seasonal directional prior for MIS on any symbol.
quote: If >=75% of profitable periods → strong trend; If 60–75% → moderate trend; If <60% → flat

mechanism: Spread value at date dt = k_Symbol1*Open(Symbol1,D1) − k_Symbol2*Open(Symbol2,D1); same multi-year month statistics and average-path overlay on the spread series. Intra-market (FX pairs, XAG−XAU, WTI−BRN) relative-price seasonality. Quality filter: ≥10–15y sample, no wild year outliers, ~70%+ same-direction years.
data_needed: Two symbols in Market Watch with long D1 history; k_Symbol1/k_Symbol2 weights; MonthToShow; YearsToShow.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: D1 spreads: XAGUSD−XAUUSD, EURUSD−GBPUSD, GBPUSD−NZDUSD, GBPUSD−XAGUSD, WTI−BRN; weights e.g. silver:gold 1:2 or 1:1.
why_new_for_mis: Weighted two-asset seasonal spread sensor—relative-price calendar regime for MIS beyond single-instrument seasonality.
quote: In the indicator, the spread is calculated as the difference between the opening prices of two instruments, with configurable weighting multipliers for each symbol
